firstLine: November travel feels like a quiet reward after the year’s rush.
"November is the month for destinations that feel like a warm embrace after the year’s chill.
Planning a trip with friends can feel like handing over your privacy to every app you use.
text:
Planning a trip with friends can feel like handing over your privacy to every app you use. 

We built Roamie so that the only data it keeps is what’s needed for the trip itself. No profiling, no trackers, no hidden details about who you are beyond what you share. 

That means no ads following you, no third parties guessing your habits, nothing stored beyond the votes, the wheel spins, and the destination chosen. It’s just a tool for deciding where to go, and nothing more. 

We don’t ask for much in return. What would you trust a tool to keep private when planning a trip?

firstLine: Planning a trip with friends often means coordinating messages, spreadsheets, and endless back-and-forth.
text:
Planning a trip with friends often means coordinating messages, spreadsheets, and endless back-and-forth. 

We built Roamie to make that easier. Anyone can join a trip with a link or a short code, no app to download, nothing to sign up for. It’s just a page in the browser, and it stays free. 

The goal was to keep it simple: no extra steps, no friction. If you’ve ever wasted time trying to get everyone on the same page, you’ll know why that matters. 

What’s the one thing that always slows down your group’s planning?

firstLine: This week’s small steps make Roamie a little more reliable for the trips that matter most.
text:
This week’s small steps make Roamie a little more reliable for the trips that matter most.

We fixed a few things that might have caused frustration when sharing a trip. If you’ve ever tried to add a video and it didn’t work, it should now. If a post looked the same two days in a row, that won’t happen again. And if you’ve ever lost track of a draft on TikTok, you’ll see where it got to before it disappeared.

The landing page now shows photos with the guide cards, so you can picture the kind of trips people are planning. And if you’ve ever wondered why a post didn’t go through, you’ll see the attempts we tried and discarded, so you know we’re not giving up.

What’s the one thing that still makes planning a trip feel like too much work?
